Role Overview

The Senior Director, Automation is a key member of the Data Analytics team, responsible for leading the delivery of automation and AI solutions, as well as analytics supporting audit engagements, across Audit & Advisory Services globally. The role combines innovation, critical thinking, technical expertise, and strong business acumen to translate audit and business needs into practical, scalable, secure, production-ready solutions that measurably enhance audit efficiency, coverage, and assurance.

You will provide leadership across solution design, development and implementation, audit analytics delivery, project execution, stakeholder management, adoption, and data and AI governance, leveraging data, analytics, automation, and AI to advance the Audit & Advisory Services strategy. This position reports to the AVP, Data Analytics, Audit & Advisory Services.

Position Responsibilities

Automation Portfolio Leadership & Delivery:

Oversee the portfolio of automation projects across the team, providing end-to-end leadership from solution design and planning through development, implementation, and hand-off.
Provide technical and functional expertise in the design of automation and analytics solutions, challenging proposed approaches and guiding the team toward practical, scalable, and sustainable solutions.
Establish project plans, estimate effort and timelines, define milestones and resource requirements, and monitor execution against agreed deliverables.
Proactively identify delivery risks, dependencies, and technical or business challenges; work with the team and stakeholders to resolve roadblocks and adjust delivery plans as required.
Maintain accountability for project execution, ensuring solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and to expected quality standards.

Portfolio Governance & Senior Management Reporting

Provide regular, transparent reporting to senior management on project status, milestones, risks, dependencies, resource requirements, and expected completion dates.
Assess project progress and viability and provide clear recommendations on the appropriate course of action, including whether to persist, pause, reprioritize, redesign, or stop an initiative.
Own and continuously improve the team's delivery framework, including intake, business requirements, solution design, stage gates, and monthly portfolio reviews.

Foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement, and disciplined execution.

University degree in computer science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or another quantitative/technical discipline; Master’s degree preferred.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

10+ years of progressive experience in data engineering, data platforms or software engineering, including 5+ years leading engineering teams, with demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale, cloud-native data platforms and leading complex agile programs.
Strong understanding of capital markets, investment management and market and reference data, including experience with major data vendors, licensing, entitlements and usage controls; private markets experience is an asset.

As the National Director, Finance, you are a key partner to the National CEO and Senior Leadership Team, responsible for the organization's financial strategy, stewardship, reporting, compliance, and risk management. You will provide clear financial insight to support decision-making, lead the Finance Team, and maintain strong systems and controls across a complex national charitable organization. This role requires a strategic leader who can also roll up their sleeves, balancing high-level advice with hands-on financial leadership and execution.
The ideal candidate is a seasoned finance leader with a proven track record in charitable or non-profit environments, strong knowledge of Canadian accounting and regulatory requirements, and experience overseeing donation receipting and fund accounting. Executive Leadership

Lead and manage the Finance Team and external financial support, ensuring clear priorities, strong performance, and reliable financial services across the organization.

Financial Leadership & Strategy

Position Overview

Nexus Energy is seeking a Vice President, Treasury to build and lead its Treasury function. Reporting directly to the CEO, the VP will manage foreign exchange and interest rate exposures, execute hedging strategies, and oversee liquidity, banking relationships, and treasury operations.
The VP will partner with Trading, Finance, Settlements, and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to manage financial exposures and develop treasury processes and controls that support growth. Treasury will operate within the company’s Risk Policy and risk appetite, which are governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.

We welcome senior corporate treasury professionals and senior banking or capital markets professionals with corporate advisory experience in hedging, funding, or liquidity. The role combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution.

What You Will Do

Foreign Exchange(FX) Risk Management
Lead the identification, measurement, monitoring, and management of the company's foreign exchange exposures. Ensure FX exposures are managed appropriately in line with the company's Risk Policy framework and in collaboration with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Evaluate and execute appropriate FX hedging instruments and strategies, including forwards, swaps, options and structured hedging solutions, where appropriate to mitigate exposures arising from trading activities, operational cash flows, cross-border transactions and foreign currency-denominated assets and liabilities.
Develop and maintain treasury-specific FX risk management processes and procedures, including exposure monitoring, hedge execution and operational controls, supporting the implementation of the company's Risk Policy framework and associated parameters as governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Monitor currency market developments and proactively advise senior leadership on material FX risks, market conditions and potential hedging opportunities.

Interest Rate (IR) Risk Management
Lead the identification, measurement, monitoring and management of the company's interest rate exposures across its balance sheet and financing activities, in accordance with the company'sRisk Policy framework and in collaboration with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Evaluate the impact of changing interest rate environments on the company's financing costs, cash flows, liquidity and overall financial position.
Develop and maintain treasury-specific interest rate risk management processes and procedures, including exposure monitoring, hedge execution and operational controls, supporting the implementation of the company's Risk Policy framework and associated parameters as governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Monitor interest rate market developments and proactively advise senior leadership on material IR risks and provide strategic advice on interest rate positioning, hedging alternatives and financing considerations.

Balance Sheet Liquidity & Cash Management
Collaborate with Finance, Settlements and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to monitor cash positions, funding requirements and liquidity buffers across the company's banking relationships and legal entities, ensuring sufficient liquidity to support ongoing trading activities, operational requirements and strategic initiatives.
Work closely with Finance, Trading, Settlements and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to anticipate material cash flow requirements, settlement obligations and potential liquidity pressures, developing and maintaining short-, medium- and long-term cash flow and liquidity forecasting frameworks.
Oversee liquidity requirements associated with trading activities, including collateral, margining, credit support arrangements and other working capital considerations.
Proactively identify opportunities to optimize cash utilization, funding efficiency, and returns on excess liquidity, as well as potential liquidity risks, and develop appropriate contingency funding and liquidity management plans.

Banking & Financial Institution Relationships
Own and manage the company's banking and financial institution relationships, acting as a primary point of contact for treasury-related matters. Develop strategic relationships with existing and potential banking partners, ensuring the company has access to appropriate banking products, credit facilities, and financial services.
Lead discussions and negotiations relating to banking arrangements, credit facilities, cash management solutions, trade finance, and other treasury-related services. Coordinate with senior leadership and the Finance team on financing requirements, facility renewals, credit negotiations, and broader funding initiatives.
Identify opportunities to diversify banking relationships, optimize banking costs, and improve access to financial products and services.
Advise the CEO and senior leadership on funding strategy and capital structure. Evaluate financing alternatives, including new or expanded credit facilities, to support trading activity, working capital, and business growth.
Partner with Finance and Legal to assess financing terms, collateral requirements, and covenant implications, and support the execution of approved financing initiatives.

Strategic Advisory & Risk Management Governance
Act as the company's senior treasury subject matter expert and provide strategic advice to the CEO and senior leadership on FX, interest rate, liquidity, and broader financial risk management matters, and recommend appropriate financial risk mitigation solutions that balance commercial objectives, risk tolerance, and market conditions within the company'sRisk Policy framework as defined and governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.

Overall Risk Policy ownership and governance will remain with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.

Establish effective working relationships with Trading, Finance, Settlements, and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to ensure financial exposures arising from business activities are appropriately identified, communicated, monitored, and managed within the company's established Risk Policy framework.
Collaborate with Trading and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to understand current and anticipated trading positions, transaction structures, forecast cash flows, and associated FX and interest rate exposures, including financial risk and hedging considerations relating to customer transactions.
Work with Finance and Settlements to identify balance sheet exposures, financing requirements, foreign currency liabilities and other financial risks, ensuring timely identification of settlement-related exposures, currency requirements, cash movements and potential liquidity mismatches.
Partner with Risk &Regulatory Affairs to support the monitoring and management of financial risk exposures and associated hedging activities, providing treasury expertise and execution support as required.

Treasury Infrastructure, Process Development & Team Enablement
Establish and develop the company's treasury function, including the implementation of appropriate processes, systems, controls and reporting infrastructure. Assess existing treasury-related workflows and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, transparency, consistency and risk oversight.
Develop standardized processes for exposure identification, hedge execution, trade capture, confirmation, settlement, reconciliation and ongoing monitoring.
Work collaboratively with Finance and Settlements to strengthen internal treasury knowledge and capabilities. Cross-train and upskill existing Finance team members in treasury operations, FX and interest rate risk management, financial instruments and hedging methodologies.
Establish appropriate documentation, procedures, and knowledge-sharing practices to reduce key-person dependency and ensure continuity of treasury operations.
Develop a scalable treasury operating model that can accommodate increased trading volumes, additional business lines, international expansion, and organizational growth.
Coordinate with Finance, Risk & Regulatory Affairs, external auditors, and other relevant stakeholders on treasury-related accounting, documentation, audit, and regulatory matters, as applicable.
Assess and implement treasury tools and reporting that improve visibility into cash balances, liquidity forecasts, financial exposures, hedge positions, and collateral requirements.

Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. A CFA, CPA, CTP, or relevant graduate degree is an asset.

Experience implementing or improving treasury systems, banking platforms, cash forecasting tools, or financial risk reporting is an asset.
Experience in energy, power trading, commodities, or another business with significant exposure to financial markets is an asset.
Demonstrated expertise and deep understanding of foreign exchange markets, FX derivatives, and corporate FX risk management, as well as interest rate markets, interest rate derivatives, and balance sheet interest rate risk management.
Experience developing and implementing financial hedging strategies and risk management frameworks and advising treasury, finance, and C-suite-level decision-makers on the relevant use of these strategies.
Strong understanding of corporate liquidity management, cash flow forecasting, banking facilities, and balance sheet management.
Experience managing banking relationships with domestic and international financial institutions.
Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with different business units, including Trading, Finance, Settlements, Risk & Regulatory Affairs and senior management.
Strong communicator with commercial acumen, negotiation skills and the ability to translate complex financial market risks into practical business recommendations. Possesses a keen ability to distil complex subject matter into digestible and actionable intelligence.
